title: 第 42 課｜帕松括號：守恆量的代數｜Landau–Lifshitz 經典力學
description:
取任何一個依賴座標、動量和時間的函數。它隨時間的全導數是對時間的偏導數，再加上對每個座標與每個動量的偏導數各自乘上它們的變化率。把哈密頓方程代進去，那些變化率就換成哈密頓量的偏導數；整理之後，全導數等於對時間的偏導數，加上一個只由 H 和 f 的偏導數組成的組合——這個組合就叫做 H 與 f 的帕松括號。於是守恆量的條件變得非常乾淨：一個量在運動中保持不變，等價於它對時間的偏導數加上它和哈密頓量的帕松括號等於零。如果這個量不顯含時間，條件就只剩下一句話：它和哈密頓量的帕松括號等於零。在相空間裡看，這表示它的等值線正好和演化的流向重合，所以沿著運動它不會改變；反過來，不守恆的量，它的等值線會橫著切過流。任何兩個量之間都可以用同樣的方式定義帕松括號：對每一對座標與動量取交叉的偏導數相減，再全部加起來。它有幾個一看就懂的性質：把兩個函數對調，括號變號；其中一個是常數時括號為零；而且對每個變數都是線性的。座標和動量彼此之間的括號特別簡單：兩個座標的括號是零，兩個動量的括號也是零，而一個動量和它自己對應的座標，括號等於一。還有一條稍微複雜但非常重要的恆等式，叫做雅可比恆等式：把三個函數依序輪換寫成三重括號，三項加起來恆等於零。由它可以推出帕松定理：如果兩個量都是運動積分，那麼它們的帕松括號也是運動積分。證明很簡單——在雅可比恆等式裡把其中一個函數取成哈密頓量，另外兩個都與 H 的括號為零，剩下那一項就必須為零。所以已知的守恆量可以互相「相乘」，生出新的守恆量。

本影片為《Landau–Lifshitz 經典力學》教學系列第 42 課（繁體中文版）。

title: Lesson 42 | Poisson Brackets: An Algebra of Conserved Quantities | Landau–Lifshitz
description:
Take any function of the coordinates, the momenta and the time. Its total time derivative is the partial derivative with respect to time, plus the derivative with respect to each coordinate and each momentum times their rates of change. Substitute Hamilton's equations and those rates become derivatives of the Hamiltonian; collecting terms, the total derivative is the partial one plus a combination built only from derivatives of H and f, and that combination is the Poisson bracket of H with f. The condition for a conserved quantity then becomes very clean: a quantity stays constant during the motion exactly when its partial derivative with respect to time plus its Poisson bracket with the Hamiltonian vanishes. If it does not contain the time explicitly, the condition reduces to a single statement: its Poisson bracket with the Hamiltonian is zero. Seen in phase space this says its level curves coincide with the direction of the flow, so it cannot change along the motion, whereas the level curves of a quantity that is not conserved cut across the flow. A Poisson bracket can be defined for any two quantities in the same way: for each pair of a coordinate and its momentum take the crossed partial derivatives and subtract, then add over all the pairs. It has several properties that can be read off at once: interchanging the two functions changes the sign, the bracket with a constant is zero, and it is linear in each of its arguments. The brackets of coordinates and momenta among themselves are particularly simple: the bracket of two coordinates is zero, the bracket of two momenta is zero, and the bracket of a momentum with its own coordinate is one. There is also a slightly more complicated but very important relation, the Jacobi identity: written as three double brackets with the three functions cyclically permuted, the three terms add to zero identically. From it follows Poisson's theorem: if two quantities are both integrals of the motion, so is their Poisson bracket. The proof is short. Take one of the three functions in the Jacobi identity to be the Hamiltonian; the brackets of the other two with H both vanish, so the remaining term must vanish as well. Known integrals of the motion can therefore be multiplied together, in this sense, to generate new ones.

Lesson 42 of the Landau–Lifshitz Classical Mechanics teaching series (English edition).
